Instead of "snake" (which triggered "cross"), I should have used "reptile" or "venom" for "fish" if grouping, or simply "aquatic" for "fish" alone. I will avoid clues that have strong associations with the remaining distractor list and, if a clue risks a distractor, I will limit the TARGETS list to only the most obvious match to prevent the partner from guessing incorrectly.

Specifically, for 'music', I guessed 'organ' (incorrect) and 'band' (correct) in separate turns, but the game ended after the first incorrect guess in the 'organ' turn, and later I only had one chance left for 'band' which I used, but the overall game state was lost due to previous inefficiencies. My strategy of guessing two words when only one is highly certain is flawed if the second word is a weak association. Next time, I will strictly prioritize the single strongest association for each target word. If I am unsure about a second word, I will guess only the one I am certain about to avoid wasting a turn on an "innocent" word. For example, for 'music', I should have guessed only 'band' immediately if 'organ' was uncertain, or verified 'organ' was a musical instrument in this specific context before pairing it. I will also re-evaluate the list for the most direct semantic link (e.g., 'band' for music, 'bed' for sleep) and avoid stretching associations like 'telescope' for 'instrument' when 'pipe' is a clearer fit, ensuring I don't waste guesses on ambiguous terms.
